intro: Mishkat is a research project that builds calculated layers upon the text of the Mushaf, presented with their evidence. Its motto is 'We Calculate and We Present': what we calculate, we present with its documentation; what we transmit, we attribute to its source; and what we infer, we label as an inference. This page explains every part of the project: what it is, how it was accomplished, and what its limitations are — so that the specialist may judge the methodology, not merely the claim.

sanad.d: Derived from the Muṣḥaf text, its morphological (Ṣarfī) tagging, the lexicons of al-Rāghib and Ibn Fāris, and semantic vectors — no interpretation is incorporated.
A verbatim text quoted from a book and attributed to its source — presented as a source, not a computation.
An inference drawn from present, computed premises, expressed probabilistically, overtly tagged, and secured on the server.
A human selection supported by appended computed evidence — it is explicitly stated that this is not a fully automated computation.

sections.title: The Foundation: Text and Data
sections.lead: A single foundational principle rendered in the browser, upon which all layers are constructed.
sections.what: The text of the Mushaf in its two scripts (Uthmani for display, and Imla'i for search and matching), along with the structure of the Surahs, Ajza', and pages, and word-by-word morphological tagging from the Quranic Arabic Corpus (QAC): Root, Lemma, Part of Speech, Number, Gender, Definiteness, Grammatical Case (I'rab), and Derivation (Ishtiqaq); for verbs: Tense, Voice (Bina'), and Form (Wazn).
sections.how: A deterministic builder (build_qkg.py) constructs the knowledge graph from original sources and verifies its structure with each build. Then, a transformer outputs the application database (monlite/SQLite), which is read in the browser without a server. The build fails if any of the canonical counts are incorrect.
sections.limits: Sources are limited and declared: QAC (GPL license), Tanzil (CC BY), and the two classical lexicons. Anything not found in these sources is excluded from the computed layers.

sections.title: Units of Context
sections.lead: The Mushaf is divided into cohesive, precisely calculated segments—a fundamental basis for all subsequent work.
sections.what: 1,325 context units covering the entire Mushaf: each unit has its range and descriptive name. Upon these, the display of topics, the reading of a verse in its segment, and the examination of connections between verses are based.
sections.how: It was built with distributed, batch-based review, then passed a frozen, protected sample before public release: 89.5% recall and 100% rejection of antonyms. The examination report is published with its results.

sections.title: Principles and Their Elaboration — The Scrutinized Network
sections.lead: The project's most extensive endeavor: every inter-verse connection meticulously examined by an independent reader, considering both contextual segments.
sections.what: A network of 9,494 directed connections and 1,312 mutual affirmations between the qualified verses of the Mushaf, identified by 'general formulation gateways' (2,537 verses), classified into four relations: Elucidation (Bayan), Example (Mithal), Recompense (Jazaa'), and Affirmation (Tawkeed). And marked with ranks: Grand Rule (Qā'idah Kubrā) and Rule (Qā'idah).
sections.how: Deterministic morphological gates filter verses with universal scope forms (all/condition/negation+indefinite/restriction/relative pronoun/legislation/collective command…), then a semantic proximity pair generator, then a distributed examination by approximately 1,660 independent examiners, each seeing their pair with its two contextual segments and judging by the test of dispensability and indispensability. Each wave has a quality gate before the next, and a swarm ledger documenting its task and outputs.
sections.limits: Verification pairs were generated by semantic proximity, and proximity identifies similarities, not subsumptions — this layer measures 'the rule and its detail' and does not claim to be comprehensive. The inventory that revealed this is published with its negative result. Thresholds were calibrated based solely on half of the frozen precision.

sections.title: Comprehensive Verses
sections.lead: Verses encompassing multiple meanings—a reviewed selection supported by appended, precisely calculated evidence.
sections.what: 82 verses across eight chapters (two batches: 50 then 32) (Tawhid · Justice and Benevolence · Social Cohesion · Recompense · Trial · Ease · Prophethood · Humanity and the Cosmos), each with its text from our database and its evidence: 'rule formulation gateways', its segment from the Mushaf, and its examined connections, if any.
sections.how: After it was proven that vectorial measures do not measure entailment (two negative experiments published), it was filtered by meaning, then the computer verified each entry: the text is retrieved from our database, not from anyone's memory, and evidence is automatically appended. What does not pass verification is not published.
sections.limits: The 'reviewed' isnad (chain of transmission) score: it is not a fully automated calculation, nor does it pass judgment on what is not mentioned within it. The list is open for expansion through review (second batch: 32 verses, 2026-07-29).

sections.title: Mishkat Themes
sections.lead: Conceptual topics are presented through segments, not isolated verses, with each segment appearing within every pertinent topic.
sections.what: 62 topics across ten chapters; each topic has its segments ordered by their distinctiveness, and within each segment, its textual evidences are highlighted. Multiple membership: a single segment appears in every topic it pertains to.
sections.how: Each topic has a definitive lexical anchor derived from its roots and words in our database, then a semantic centroid from the average of the anchors' vectors. Contextual units are then measured against it, and what stands out from the background of all segments is taken (z ≥ 2.2) — without external calls or cost.
sections.limits: Concept seeds are selected through human review (guided by established indexing conventions), and subsequent computation is automated and deterministic. Two negative experiments were recorded: an absolute proximity threshold included the entire Qur'an in every topic, and broad seeds distorted topics — consequently, the metric was corrected, and twenty-two seeds were refined.

sections.title: Terms of Revelation: Nuances, Facets, and Roots
sections.lead: Four distinct layers address a singular inquiry: 'Why this specific word in this particular context?'
sections.what: "Differences in Revelation" (Furūq al-Tanzīl): pairs of similar verses (mutashābihāt) with literal alignment by difference category and degree of correspondence. "Linguistic Differences" (Furūq al-Lughawiyyah): a network of semantic roots, the closest roots to a given root, and its fields. "Facets and Analogues" (al-Wujūh wa al-Naẓā'ir): a polysemous word with its facets and their textual evidences. "Roots and Their Meanings" (al-Judhūr wa Ma'ānīhā): every root with its occurrences and meaning from al-Raghib and Ibn Faris, along with "Precise Count" (al-'Add al-Daqīq).
sections.how: Literal alignment is deterministic (a Lamma-level (lemma) alignment algorithm). Each pair is named by its identified differences — precedence, form, substitution, and addition — and can be queried by any of them. The root network is calculated from co-occurrence and semantic fields. The facets are transferred from dictionaries with their examples. Precise counting outputs for each root its rows (Lamma × form) with their positions and orthographic variants.
sections.limits: A published designation was corrected: more than half of the difference pairs (1,122 out of 2,019) were under a single vague name, 'complex differences' (furūq murakkabah), which was not a type of difference but rather the remainder beyond a type — these were resolved into their specific types without affecting any single pair. And 'Precise Counting' (al-ʿadd al-daqīq) declares three distinct counts: the count of the root with its derivatives, the count of the lemma (lammah) with its form, and the count of the orthography (rasm) as written — thus, a single question has three different correct answers.

sections.title: The Elucidation — Contemplating the Language of the Quran
sections.lead: Entries integrating a calculated usage map with attributed readings from eminent linguists, alongside its structured library.
sections.what: Cards for each pair or formulation: a usage map computed from the entire Mushaf (occurrences, morphology, collocations, and divergence signature), then readings of proper nouns attributed with their text, then a bridge to their sources from the nine books of Bayan (Elucidation).
sections.how: The nine books (Al-Furooq by Al-Askari · Basair by Al-Fayrouzabadi · Al-Wujuh by Al-Askari · Qamus by Al-Damghani · Nuzhat Ibn Al-Jawzi · Durrat Al-Iskafi · Malak Al-Ta'weel · Al-Burhan · Al-Itqan) were structured entry by entry from authenticated copies, and their entries were linked to roots and positions. The cards are of two types: twenty edited with review, and 432 automatically generated, tagged as such.
sections.limits: Readings of proper nouns (aʿlām) are quoted verbatim and attributed to their sources — they are not presented as our own computation. Automatically generated cards are explicitly labeled 'without editing or justification'.

sections.title: Reference Library
sections.lead: Forty-three cited works, including twenty venerable tafsirs, are retrieved surah by surah upon demand.
sections.what: Accessible and classical Tafsir (exegeses), Asbab al-Nuzul (occasions of revelation), Qira'at (readings), I'rab (grammatical analysis), books of Bayan (elucidation), and the two lexicons — all quoted, attributed to their authors, and presented as is, separate from the computed layers.
sections.how: Lightweight books are shipped with the application. The twenty canonical ones (Al-Tabari, Ibn Kathir, Al-Qurtubi, Al-Razi, Al-Kashshaf, Ibn Ashour…) are divided into a file per surah on a public data repository; their surah is fetched upon request and cached — "Sound Mode". Twenty-two of them are embedded with vectors for semantic Nibras search — including the nine complete books of elucidation (completed 2026-07-29) — and the answer adheres to the principle of "one book per science" to avoid repetition.

sections.title: Research
sections.lead: A singular engine locates any verse, regardless of its transcription, operating without a server.
sections.what: Text search with layers tagged by prominence (Phrase · All words · Approximation · Root), and semantic search on pre-loaded vectors, scanned locally, and a search box that understands "Al-Baqarah 255", "Juz' 15", and "Ayat al-Kursi".
sections.how: An Arabic analyzer normalizes the forms of hamza, taa, and alif maqsurah, removes attached prefixes (wa, fa, bi, ka, li, and al with their structures) and pronominal suffixes, and builds a structural key without long vowels — above it, an inverted index in the browser by relevance order. Thus, whoever types "fa'aktharuhum" or "wa'aktharuhum" or "aktharuhum" finds the verse, and whoever types "al-rahman" or "qari'" or "ibrahim" finds it as well.
sections.limits: Normalization is symmetrical for both query and text, thus it does not introduce elements extraneous to the query — and root expansion is an independent option that does not conflate with text results.

sections.title: Intelligent Mishkat (Nibras)
sections.lead: A search function that independently invokes Mishkat's tools and responds with securely attributed results from the server.
sections.what: A conversational assistant with eleven tools operating on project data: semantic search, roots, context units, Tafsir and Asbab al-Nuzul for a verse, Mishkat layers, deterministic count, and draft composition. The tools are executed in the user's browser on local data, free of charge.
sections.how: A stateless tool loop: the model requests a tool, which the browser executes and returns its result until a final answer is generated by a stronger model. Above it are guardians on the server: the verse text is only written as a literal transcription from a tool's result, and attributed quotations likewise. Numbers are transferred from the layers and not estimated, and inference requires presented premises, a probability formula, and a set of bounds.
sections.limits: The answer is free in its phrasing but constrained by facts; there is no fatwa (religious edict) or preference given in disagreements, and hadith (prophetic tradition) is only mentioned within the text of a retrieved source. A fixed set of probes (25 live probes) is re-run before any change in the guardians (ḥurrās), and a frozen question bank passed 94.8% above the 90% benchmark with zero factual fabrication.

sections.title: Methodology and Operational Guidelines
sections.lead: Our methodology for verification, correction, and publication in the event of experimental failure.
sections.what: A phrase charter that governs terminology (verification is on our work, not on the text itself), documentation of each batch in a ledger detailing its mission, inputs, and outputs, thresholds announced before each batch, protected samples frozen before review, and negative results published as is.
sections.how: Each layer has a deterministic generator that, when re-run, produces the same result. Every number in the interface is transferred from the build outputs, not manually entered. Errors are publicly corrected with their history and not erased — including the correction of the Qawa'id (rules) layer name after an inventory proved it does not measure Jawami' al-Kalim (concise comprehensive expressions), and the correction of the topics measure after a negative experiment.

open: Deepening Waves (2-7) are not yet operational: This will involve invoking the connections, then updating the tag, re-examining the preserved sample, and recording the difference.

The 'Comprehensive Verses' have reached 82 in two installments and remain extensible upon review; the automated detection of inclusion requires an independent examination of the portal qualifiers (2,537), not of neighboring pairs.
Section on Revelation Variants: Its composite is under review — either to be fixed for functionality or to be removed.
The display of the Elucidation Section is undergoing redesign to be more useful for the non-specialist.
